siteSource.lessons: year11/applications-of-measurement/lesson01 (formulas and units), lesson02 (area of basic shapes), lesson03 (Pythagoras), lesson04 (perimeter and arc length), lesson05 (sectors, annuli, composite; its sine area rule is Year 12 t09), lesson06 (surface area of prisms and cylinders), lesson07 (surface area of spheres and composites), lesson08 (volume of prisms and cylinders), lesson09 (volume of pyramids, cones and spheres), lesson12 (mass section only; its energy section is Year 12 r14), lesson13 (trapezoidal rule). lesson10 (scale drawings, Year 12 r04) and lesson11 (errors and limits of accuracy) carry no 2024 Year 11 point.

recommendations: Run a01 to a11 in outline order, playlist numbers 37 to 47, straight after m09 (36). a05 splits into a05a (straight-edged shapes) and a05b (circles, arcs, sectors and curved composites), both at playlist 41, because one point covers seven shape families plus perimeter and composites and cannot be taught well under 570 s (ruling 8's test). Root to confirm the split.

Joins: a01 opens on m09's final frame exactly (coin jar with '100 c = $1', coded tape strip '10 mm = 1 cm', grey chip 'Managing money: done', chips 'Next: units of measurement', '?'); m09's provisional mark can be lifted. Each later video opens on the previous video's final frame. a11 closes the strand ('Applications of measurement: done') and hands to math-s11-t01 (provisional until t01 is designed).

Each 'Next' chip quotes the next video's on-screen heading: a01 'Units of measurement: length, mass and capacity'; a02 'Units of area and volume'; a03 'Volume and capacity'; a04 'Prefixes and powers of ten'; a05a 'Perimeter and area'; a05b 'Circles, arcs and sectors'; a06 'Pythagoras' theorem'; a07 'Irregular blocks of land'; a08 'Surface area'; a09 'Volume of prisms and cylinders'; a10 'Pyramids, cones and spheres'; a11 'The trapezoidal rule'.

Strand colour roles (fixed a01 to a11): given measurements (lengths, radii, heights) blue; conversion factor, fraction of a circle, the 1/2 or 1/3 amber; area and surface teal; volume and capacity olive; removed, hidden or internal parts violet; answer green; mistake red (crossed slips only).

Recurring models introduced once: the unit ladder with multiply and divide arrows (a01; squared and cubed rungs in a02; the volume-capacity bridge in a03; the prefix ladder in a04); the grid square and unit-cube fill (a02, reused a03); 'Plan first: Area = ... + ... - ...' written before numbers (a05a, reused a05b, a07, a08 face list, a09, a10); the exposed or hidden face list (a08); the slice stack V = Ah (a09, reused a10 and a11); the strip builder for the trapezoidal rule (a11).

Memory aids introduced once: a01 'Smaller unit, more of them: multiply. Bigger unit, fewer of them: divide.'; a02 'Square the length factor for area. Cube it for volume.'; a03 'A 1 cm cube holds 1 mL. A 1 m cube holds 1000 L, a kilolitre.'; a04 'Capitals are huge: M, G, T. Lower case is small: m, µ, n (and c). Except k, a thousand.'; a05a 'Every area is base times perpendicular height, or half of it.'; a05b 'Take theta over 360 of the whole circle.'; a06 'Longest side: square, add, square root. Shorter side: square, subtract, square root.'; a07 'Split it, label it, add it. Fence only the outside.'; a08 'List every face, cross out the hidden ones, then add.'; a09 'Volume = area of the end x length.'; a10 'Pointy solids hold a third.'; a11 'Average the two ends, times the gap.'

Everyday anchors (no people, hands or faces; no science contexts): a ribbon, a fun run, a produce scale, a ute load, a water jug, a tank and a farm dam (a01); floor tiles, a paddock, netball courts and a block cube (a02); a fish tank, a backyard pool and an Olympic pool (a03); a phone's storage, camera and processor (a04); a lawn, a triangular garden bed, an angled parking bay and a sail (a05a); a pizza, a round cake, a running track and a pond path (a05b); a softball diamond, a flying-fox ladder, a phone screen, a gate brace and a ramp (a06); a house block and a paddock plan (a07); a cereal box, a food tin, a golf ball, a polytunnel and a bollard (a08); the cereal box again, a concrete ramp, the water tank, a sloping pool, a retaining wall (a09); an ice-cream cone, a skylight, a watermelon, a sand pile and a bowl (a10); a land block, a garden pond, a drainage channel and a garden bed (a11).

Prices: water $2.70 per kL is m07's labelled example; concrete $220 per cubic metre is the site's example and is labelled 'example price' (Codex finds a dated NSW source or reports). No other price is used.

Facts Codex confirms in the error check: netball court 30.5 m x 15.25 m; softball base paths 18.29 m (shown as 18.3 m); golf ball minimum diameter 42.67 mm; Olympic pool 50 m x 25 m with a minimum depth of 2 m; printer paper about 0.1 mm thick; the trapezoidal rule printed on the 2024 Standard reference sheet.
Pace flags: a01 and a07 are full; a02 and a08 near 9 minutes; a05 split (see above). No other split proposed.
Header strip (owner rule of 23 Nov): the focus area only, 'APPLICATIONS OF MEASUREMENT'.

entries.mainLearnerQuestion: How do we convert between units of length, mass and capacity?

syllabusActions.text: Identify and convert between the metric units of length: millimetres (mm), centimetres (cm), metres (m) and kilometres (km)
Identify and convert between the metric units of mass: milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg) and tonnes (t)
Identify and convert between the metric units of capacity: millilitres (mL), litres (L), kilolitres (kL) and megalitres (ML)

entries.stopBoundary: The length ladder mm, cm, m, km; prefixes milli, centi, kilo as their meanings; multiply to a smaller unit, divide to a bigger one; units matching before a calculation; mass mg, g, kg, t and capacity mL, L, kL, ML in steps of 1000. Not: area and volume units (a02), volume to capacity (a03), powers of ten (a04).
